description: Show how many credits a generation would use before it starts, so the user can agree to it. Inputs it would refuse to run come back as a refusal instead.

actor_ids.description: The cast, lead first. A remake (video_swap or trend_remake) takes exactly one actor, who replaces the main person in the clip. A story casts up to 3 cartoons saved to its brand.

asset_ids.description: Motion graphics (workflow_type animated) only: the library files the composition shows. Every other lane refuses them; a prompt_video takes files as references instead.

auto_approve.description: Story only: render the storyboard as soon as it is ready, on one quote charged at create: the storyboard plus a render estimated from target_duration. Once the storyboard exists, a lower render quote is refunded and a higher one is charged.

caption_preset.description: Captions edit only (video_edit, edit_kind captions): the look of the burned-in captions. Every other lane ignores it.

captions.description: Story only: burn the spoken words into the video as it is made. Every other lane refuses it; caption a finished video instead with a video_edit generation, edit_kind captions and source_workflow_id set to it.

characters.description: The characters a format invents its cast from, such as the foods in a Talking Food video. Each entry is either {"key": "<one of the video type cast_choices keys>"} or {"text": "<your own, in a few words>"}. Only a format that declares cast_choices takes them.

format.description: Story only, on an illustrated look: how the story is told. explainer tells it one short line a scene, cutting straight from one to the next, one big word at a time, with every scene moving, from 15 to 60 seconds. Leave it out for the usual telling. The price is quoted before anything is made.

motion.description: Story only, on an illustrated look: which scenes get a moving picture made from their own painting. none leaves every scene still, key moves the opening, the peaks and the ending (about a third of the scenes), all moves every painted scene. Left out, the look decides: all for documentary collage, key for the rest. A clip costs about 2 credits a second, 7 at the four-second floor, and is quoted with the storyboard before anything is made. With auto_approve there is no storyboard to quote, so create holds the most clips the scene budget allows at 15 seconds each (24 credits a clip); the unused part comes back as soon as the storyboard is set.

music.description: The soundtrack. A story takes auto to let us pick a track, compose for one written for it, upload for one of your own, or none. Every other lane takes library, upload or none.

previous_id.description: Story only: a finished story of this brand that this one continues as its next part, with its cast, look and meters.

references.description: The files a prompt_video works from, each called in the prompt as @ and its name: images, video clips (30 seconds in all, cut with trim [start, end] in seconds) and audio. Source upload takes the editor_asset id get_upload returns once the upload is ready, actor an actor id, product a product id, link the source_url of a video_reference upload, result a finished prompt_video generation id.

resolution.description: The resolution the video renders at, 720p unless named. A prompt video takes 480p or 720p; a remake (video_swap or trend_remake) renders at 720p only and refuses any other.

seconds.description: How much of the video to keep, from start. A remake (video_swap or trend_remake) keeps 4 to 30 seconds, the first 15 unless start and seconds name another part, and refuses a longer one. An animated video takes seconds as its length.

sfx.description: Story only: add sound effects under each scene. Every other lane refuses it.

source_id.description: Story only: a finished story of this brand to open again at its storyboard, at no charge, and render again once edited and approved.

source_url.description: The link the generation starts from: the web page a launch animation reads, or the video a trend remake, composed video or video swap copies. Either way, one the user made or has the rights to use.

spoken_script.description: Story with a format that offers it: the exact words to say, kept to the letter and cut into one line a scene. Under two minutes, about 280 words. Leave it out to have the script written from the brief. Every other lane reads it as the words an actor speaks; with two or more actors, open each speaker's turn with their actor token and a colon, numbered in actor_ids order: @actor_1: Ready? @actor_2: Always.

style.description: Story only: the look, drawn on a skin or illustrated in a preset.

swap_who.description: Remake only: who in the video the actor replaces, in your own words, such as "the woman in the red coat". Leave it out to replace the main person.

vote_winner.description: Story only, with previous_id: the option that won the vote the previous part ended on.
